### FOURTH.

shining, indeed dark and livid with deathly earthiness.
The <term>Moon</term> <gloss>silver</gloss> is also turned yellow <term>citrinatur</term> <gloss>made citrine or golden-hued</gloss> in a similar way with the solution of <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron</gloss>.
The method of <term>citrination</term> <gloss>the process of turning golden-yellow</gloss> for that which is accomplished through <term>Vitriol</term> <gloss>a sulfate mineral</gloss> or <term>Cuperosa</term> <gloss>copper sulfate/vitriol</gloss> is such as this. Let a certain quantity of each of these be taken, and let that part which suffers sublimation be sublimed until it is sublimed in total with extraction; after this, however, let that which has been sublimed be sublimed again with the mode of fire appropriate to it, so that something is fixed from it, part after part, until the greater part of it is fixed. Afterward, let it be administered with the intent of caution regarding the fire, so that a greater fire may be administered to it for perfection. After this, let it be dissolved into a most <term>rubicund</term> <gloss>red</gloss> water, to which there is no equal. Then, indeed, you shall use ingenuity so that you may provide it with an entrance into the <term>Lunar body</term> <gloss>the substance of silver</gloss>, and these ingenuities have been sufficiently shown to you if you are a seeker of the perfect work which we have written. And because we see that the things of this kind adhere in a friendly manner to the depth of the <term>Moon</term>, we have therefore considered, and it is certain, that these are of their root, and therefore it happens that they are altered through them. These, indeed, are all the medicines of the first order which we have brought forward; nevertheless, many modes of them can be multiplied, while preserving the essence of the <term>pigmental</term> <gloss>coloring</gloss> things in the variety of the modes. Some, however, have discovered many more medicines, but it happens that one of two things necessarily occurs, because it is necessary that they create the medicine either from the same things, or from those having the same nature. Or they compose a medicine which is equivalent to that which does not exist, with its own alteration, and which confers nothing to the world, nor to the parts of the world, until the mover in the sublime, mobile nature of things has rested, incorrupt.

<summary>This page continues the alchemical instructions for "citrination," focusing on using vitriol and copper-based minerals to induce a golden color in silver. It emphasizes the necessity of careful fire management, sublimation, and chemical fixation to achieve a stable result.</summary>
